questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It had to be outside of Europe and have a good amount of offered courses within my field of interest.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: A bit difficult. The websites are not that easy to navigate, and info regarding e.g. vaccines were hard to come by.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A lot of emails. You do receive most reminders of deadlines, updates etc. on email. There's also a mandatory online meeting with info.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: A lot of the info from the online meeting wasn't that useful to me, a lot of it was about finding a job.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy. I just went on Facebook, they have a bunch of groups. Obviously beware of scammers, but there were many offers. UCSD also has a website you can use, but it only had a few ads.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's cheaper than living on campus. I was very lucky and lived with four American girls from the same uni, so it was amazing. But you lose some of that "international" vibe that I-House brings - like going on trips.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Extremely expensive! The cheapest on campus housing I was offered was ~1700 USD. My off campus housing was 925 USD.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It's more confusing than at UCPH. You get an alloted timeslot, and have to work out the schedule yourself. Most courses above course code 99 have prerequisites, so you need to make en EASy request and can't apply for the course until it's been approved. Once you're approved, you can enroll during your timeslot - but it's first come first serve, so have backup courses ready.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I don't know, I didn't use any help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
I mostly got what I wanted with a few exceptions because they were so popular. But UCSD has so many courses so you'll always be able to find something else.
I had physics and chemistry of the ocean, marine microbiology, coastal ecology, ocean acidification, chemistry of the atmosphere and ocean, and satellite remote sensing. Any lab course is very competitive, so have backups for those.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Send out a lot of EASy requests, because not all professors are fast at approving you. For the most part I just wrote that I had the required courses during high school, and it worked.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very interesting courses!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All my courses were bachelor level and between course code 100-199, except for one course (satellite remote sensing) which was a mixed class of BA and MA.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It's much more like being back in high school. Mandatory attendance and multiple quizzes and assignments each week. The grade was also a split between these things, so e.g. 20% from your final, 20% from the midtmerm, 5% from attendance, and 55% quizzes and assignments.
The lectures were much shorter, either 50 minutes or 1 hour and 20 minutes. Discussion sessions were extremely easy and didn't add anything at all.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
SIO119 Physics and Chemistry of the Ocean
SIO126 Marine Microbiology
ENVR120 Coastal Ecology
SIO174 Chemistry of the Atmosphere and Ocean
SIO143 Ocean Acidification
SIO135 Satellite Remote Sensing

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: SIO119 and SIO143 are very interesting if you like the ocean! Also great professors. ENVR120 is amazing because you go on a field trip every week, and the homework is minimal.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: They have fees for everything, so you have to pay a lot of weird fees for your semester. Also not unexpected, but tax is not included in the prices shown in stores.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and rent is more expensive than in Denmark. Coffee is less expensive haha. A lot of everyday items are also cheaper. It's really just food and rent that's crazy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have a club for absolutely everything; hiking, surfing, DJ'ing, dancing, furries, religion, bookclubs, keyboards, cooking etc. I was in the administration of a student run magazine.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sign up for a club or two, doesn't even matter which ones. Attend some of the events hosted by the university.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the area and the surrounding towns. Hike. Surf. Chill. If you're up for a longer trip (an 8 hour drive), Yosemite National Park is amazing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Everyone is very sweet and welcoming, so it's not that difficult to strike up conversation.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How open and welcoming they are.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) Start preparing as soon as you can - vaccines, visa etc. There are so many deadlines before arrival. 2) Find people to hang out with and work with in class, it makes it so much more enjoyable. 3) Chill! There are a lot of courses to choose from and a lot of people to meet! It'll be fine.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Download the Pronto app for taking public transit! It's just like Rejseplanen. Get an American bank account so you can get either Zelle or Venmo, as it's what everyone uses.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the friends I made. Honestly unrivaled.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Traveling. I don't have a drivers license, and since I lived with Americans from the area, they weren't that interested in exploring. You can get around pretty easily by bus and trolley in the university area, but if you wanna go to another city, you need a drivers license. Find someone who wants to explore. That's my only regret.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
